problem_text:
A logistics coordinator needs to assign shipments to identical cargo planes. Shipments:
* Component Alpha: size 51 cubic meters
* Component Beta: size 53 cubic meters
* Component Gamma: size 33 cubic meters
* Component Delta: size 54 cubic meters
* Component Epsilon: size 51 cubic meters
* Component Zeta: size 41 cubic meters
* Component Eta: size 48 cubic meters
* Component Theta: size 60 cubic meters
* Component Iota: size 32 cubic meters
* Component Kappa: size 64 cubic meters
* Component Lambda: size 62 cubic meters
* Component Mu: size 49 cubic meters
* Component Nu: size 50 cubic meters
* Component Xi: size 47 cubic meters
* Component Omicron: size 69 cubic meters
* Component Pi: size 70 cubic meters
* Component Rho: size 50 cubic meters
* Component Sigma: size 34 cubic meters
* Component Tau: size 52 cubic meters
* Component Upsilon: size 31 cubic meters
* Component Phi: size 58 cubic meters
* Component Chi: size 69 cubic meters
* Component Psi: size 41 cubic meters
* Component Omega: size 52 cubic meters
* Component Ares: size 69 cubic meters
* Component Zeus: size 48 cubic meters
* Component Hera: size 46 cubic meters
* Component Poseidon: size 61 cubic meters
* Component Apollo: size 30 cubic meters
* Component Artemis: size 58 cubic meters
* Component Athena: size 40 cubic meters
* Component Hermes: size 45 cubic meters
* Component Dionysus: size 52 cubic meters

Each cargo plane has a maximum capacity of 100 cubic meters. Assign all shipments using the fewest planes possible. Each shipment must be loaded onto exactly one plane, and the total volume in any plane cannot exceed its capacity limit.
